query: Are Hot Rod and The Memory of Our People both magazines?

pipeline_result.response: No, the two articles are not related to each other in any way. They are separate publications with different titles and content. The article "Hot Rod" is a magazine published in Rosario, Argentina, while the article "The Memory of Our People" is a magazine published in Santa Fe, Argentina.
retrieved_context: The Memory of Our People: The Memory of Our People is a magazine published in the Argentine city of Rosario, a province of Santa Fe.  The magazine was founded in 2004.  Its original title in Spanish is "La Memoria de Nuestro Pueblo".
Hot Rod (magazine): Hot Rod is a monthly American car magazine devoted to hot rodding, drag racing, and muscle cars — modifying automobiles for performance and appearance.

Hot Rod (film): Hot Rod is a 2007 American comedy film co-written, directed by, and starring members of The Lonely Island (Andy Samberg, Jorma Taccone and Akiva Schaffer).  The film stars Samberg as an amateur stuntman whose abusive step-father, Frank (Ian McShane) continuously mocks and disrespects him.  When Frank grows ill, Rod raises money for his heart operation by executing his largest stunt yet.  In addition to raising money for the operation, he also does so to win Frank's respect, by kicking his butt.  The film also stars Taccone, Sissy Spacek, Will Arnett, Danny McBride, Isla Fisher and Bill Hader.  It was directed by Schaffer (in his directorial debut) and distributed by Paramount Pictures.
